title: Best Ecommerce Performance Creative Agencies for Meta Ads (2026)
summary: Compare eight ecommerce performance creative agencies for Facebook and Instagram by the job each fits, published scope and minimums. Checked Oct 2026.
body_markdown:
## Which agencies specialize in creator and UGC-style ads?


### inBeat: creator-led ads with structured testing


As of October 2026,[inBeat's performance creative page](https://inbeat.agency/performance-creative-agency) lists creator sourcing and vetting, high-velocity ad variant production, and hook, angle and format testing, and it also lists whitelisting and paid amplification, Meta ads management and TikTok ads management. Its FAQ lists "standalone performance creative services" among the work it takes on.[inBeat's DTC marketing page](https://inbeat.agency/dtc-marketing-agency) says vetted micro-influencers produce unboxing videos, testimonials, product demos and lifestyle shots, and that brands get full rights to reuse the assets. Pricing is not published. Our[UGC agencies comparison](https://knowlify.com/articles/best-ugc-agencies) covers inBeat's separate UGC service next to other creator agencies.


**Consider it when** you want real creators on camera, plan to run the media yourself or with inBeat, and want each batch built around testing hooks and angles.


### StreetTalk: one specialist format


As of October 2026,[StreetTalk](https://www.streettalk.com/) makes unscripted street-interview ads for consumer brands. It films in Los Angeles, New York and Miami, with the city chosen by the target demographic. Every brief ships two angles built to be tested against each other, hooks are cut in several versions, and assets are packaged for partnership ads, whitelisting and every placement. The site states that "StreetTalk does not buy media," and its headline says "Authentic reactions are 15 days away." Pricing is not published.


**Consider it when** you already have a main creative partner or media buyer and want to add a format built on real strangers reacting to your product.


## Which options suit studio production or a creative subscription?


### Pilothouse Studios: shoots for established DTC brands


As of October 2026,[Pilothouse Studios](https://www.pilothouse.co/studios) , a service line of the performance marketing agency Pilothouse Digital, lists direct response ads, commercials, explainer videos, motion graphics, ecommerce and lifestyle photography, and creator content from in-house creators and a creator network, under the line "We make it, you own it." The[Pilothouse homepage](https://www.pilothouse.co/) says the agency "is built for established, ambitious DTC ecommerce brands," lists an office in Victoria, British Columbia, names Meta ads (Facebook and Instagram) among the platforms it manages, and prices through monthly retainers, performance-based incentives and custom project scopes. The studio page does not say whether the studio can be hired for creative only.


**Consider it when** your ads need product photography and filmed production as well as edited video.


### Superside: a creative subscription on an annual term


As of October 2026,[Superside's pricing page](https://www.superside.com/pricing) says subscriptions "start at a $15,000 monthly minimum on an annual term," with a dedicated team from $30,000 a month on a 12-month term.[Superside's ad creative page](https://www.superside.com/ad-creative) names Meta, TikTok and LinkedIn among its social platforms and covers static design, motion graphics and video production, with "multiple variants fast" for testing. Neither page says Superside buys media or manages campaigns, and the ad creative page does not mention UGC.


**Consider it when** your marketing team wants one creative partner across ads, design and other channels and can commit to an annual term.


## Why does an ecommerce brand on Meta need a steady flow of new creative?


Meta's own engineering writing explains why variety matters. Its[Meta engineering post on Andromeda](https://engineering.fb.com/2024/12/02/production-engineering/meta-andromeda-advantage-automation-next-gen-personalized-ads-retrieval-engine/) , Meta's personalized ads retrieval engine, describes the retrieval stage as "selecting ads from tens of millions of ad candidates into a few thousand relevant ad candidates," and says the number of ad creatives in Meta's recommendation systems is expected to grow significantly. The same post notes that "increased ad diversity can improve people's experience with ads and drive better advertiser outcomes."


For an online store, that makes distinct concepts (a different buyer, problem or proof point) more useful than resized copies of one ad, so ask each agency how many new concepts a batch contains. Our[ad creative testing framework](https://knowlify.com/articles/ad-creative-testing) shows one way to plan those batches.


Format matters too. Meta's[Reels ads guidance](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/facebook-instagram-reels-ads) says Reels ads with key messages in the safe zone, quality audio and vertical video see better results, and reports 2x higher delivery to the Reels placement for campaigns that included 9:16 video ads with audio and key messages in the safe zone. Ask each agency for vertical cuts with sound designed in. For format ideas by product type, see our guide to[ecommerce video ads](https://knowlify.com/articles/ecommerce-video-ads) .


Creator ads add one more choice. Meta's[partnership ads documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/blog/post/2025/03/25/instagram-partnership-ads/) says partnership ads "allow advertisers to run ads with creators, brands, and other businesses," with the advertiser and partner accounts featured in the ad's header. If that format is central to your plan, pick an agency that works with real creators and handles their permissions.


## Which agencies make short-form video ads for ecommerce?


Every agency on the shortlist makes video ads, but they differ in who appears on camera and how fast batches arrive. Meta's Reels guidance above favors vertical video with sound, so ask each one for 9:16 cuts. By published scope (as of October 2026):


Agency Video ads it lists Who is on camera Published volume or pace


Knowlify AI UGC, 3D character animation and AI commercials AI presenters About 25 finished ads a week; first batch about five days after kickoff


Common Thread Collective UGC ads in packages of 20, 40 or 80, plus branded ads from your asset library Real creators, 5 to 20 per package Three to four weeks per UGC batch, seven days per branded batch


TubeScience In-house studio video, including partnership ads on Meta Not stated Not published


Darkroom Motion, UGC and AI formats alongside statics Not stated 250 to 600 assets per cycle, delivered every two weeks


inBeat Unboxing videos, testimonials, product demos and lifestyle shots, with hook, angle and format variants Vetted micro-influencers Not published


StreetTalk Unscripted street-interview ads, two angles per brief, several hook versions Real people interviewed on the street Its headline puts reactions 15 days away


Pilothouse Studios Direct response ads, commercials, explainer videos, motion graphics and creator content In-house creators and a creator network Not published


Superside Motion graphics and video production, with multiple variants for testing Not stated; its ad creative page does not mention UGC Not published


Two AI video providers outside the shortlist also publish short-form video scope for online stores. We checked their own sites on October 30, 2026:


- **[Admiral Media's AI UGC service](https://admiral.media/ai-ugc-agency/)** makes AI-generated UGC ads "for apps and ecommerce brands," using AI presenters with human editing and quality review. Batches run from €10,000 for 20 ads of up to 15 seconds to €29,000 for 80 ads of up to 60 seconds, in 9:16, 1:1 and 4:5. It says its ideal clients invest US$50,000 or more a month in paid media, and that campaign and budget management must be agreed separately.
- **[EditClub](https://www.editclub.co/)** describes itself as an on-demand creative team for DTC brands spending $10K or more a month on Meta. It generates UGC-style actors, product shots and B-roll with AI video models, with no cameras or creators, and delivers 9:16, 1:1 and 16:9 versions cut for TikTok, Reels, YouTube and Meta ads. Plans start at $1,600 a month, and it lists a first edit in 48 hours.


If the ad needs a real person handling the product, choose an agency with real people on camera, such as CTC, inBeat, StreetTalk or Pilothouse Studios. If you need many concepts and hooks a week without a creator roster, Knowlify, Admiral Media and EditClub make their presenters with AI.


## How should you compare quotes from ecommerce creative agencies?


Most agencies in this list quote privately, so ask every finalist to price the same unit: finished ads you can run, with the rights you need, delivered by a date.


Line item What to ask


New concepts How many distinct ideas are in each batch, not counting resizes or hook swaps


Variations Which part changes: hook, caption, length or aspect ratio


Talent Real creators, street interviews, actors or AI presenters, and who approves product claims


Usage rights Paid and organic use, duration and partnership ads permissions


Turnaround When the first batch arrives and the cadence after that


Media Who runs the ads, and in whose ad account


Commitment and exit Monthly minimum, term length, and what happens to the ads and raw files if you stop


The published numbers in this guide measure different things. As of October 2026, CTC counts ads per UGC package, Darkroom counts assets per cycle, Superside publishes a monthly minimum and TubeScience ties pay to performance. Turn every proposal into cost per new concept and cost per finished ad before you compare.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick for weekly AI-made video ads for Meta, with or without campaign management; choose a creator agency when real people must appear on camera.
- For other jobs, choose by fit: creative tied to media buying, high-volume multichannel assets, creator ads, one specialist format, studio shoots or a subscription.
- As of October 2026, most agencies in this list do not publish prices; Superside's $15,000 monthly minimum and TubeScience's pay-for-performance model are the exceptions.
- Compare quotes on new concepts, variations, rights, turnaround and who runs the ads.
- Meta's Reels guidance favors vertical video with sound, and its engineers link ad diversity to better outcomes, so ask how each batch delivers both.


## FAQ


### What does an ecommerce creative agency do?


It plans and produces the ads an online store runs, such as UGC-style videos, product demos, statics and motion graphics, usually in batches built for testing. Some also run the campaigns; others, such as StreetTalk as of October 2026, only make the ads.


### How much does an ecommerce ad creative agency cost?


Most agencies in this comparison quote privately. As of October 2026, Superside publishes a $15,000 monthly minimum on an annual term, TubeScience describes a pay-for-performance model, and CTC lists ad counts per UGC package without prices. Knowlify quotes on a 30-minute call. Media spend is always separate.


### Should the creative agency also run my Meta ads?


If you have no media buyer, one team for both avoids a handoff between the people who make the ads and the people who read the results. If you have a buyer you trust, a creative-only partner such as StreetTalk, inBeat's standalone service or Knowlify's creative-only option keeps the account with your team.


### Can AI-made ads replace creator UGC for an online store?


AI-made ads can cover many concepts and hooks at volume, which supports the ad diversity Meta's engineers link to better advertiser outcomes. They cannot replace a real customer's testimonial or an ad that runs from a creator's account. Do not script an AI presenter to claim personal use of a product.


### Is Knowlify an ecommerce creative agency?


Knowlify is a done-for-you AI ads agency for Facebook and Instagram. It makes AI UGC, 3D character animation and AI commercial video ads, about 25 a week, and can manage campaigns or deliver creative only. It does not supply human creators or photo shoots.
